# dsh-minimal-router · v2.0.0
> **Give the model only the tools it needs right now.** Fixed prefix, variable tail.
## How it runs (the 30-second version)
Two entry points, everything else is bookkeeping:
| When | Hook | What happens |
| A user message arrives | `agent/inbox/claimed` | detect the stage → **4 gates**: context size → co

st payback → hysteresis → apply → `restrict()` |
| Before every tool call | `tools/pre-execute` | al
ways-allow list → lint → out-of-stage check → allow / deny |
**The four gates** (in code order; the first one that fires ends the round):
1. **Context gate** — over `contextGuardThreshold` (100k) any automatic switch is refused (`force: t

rue` still works)
2. **Cost gate** — `payback > switchPaybackTurns` (3) → refuse; explicit switches

skip this
3. **Hysteresis** — 2 confirmations + 60s cooldown before a switch sticks
4. **Apply** — `
applyStage()` → `refreshRestriction()` → `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ deny })`
**The per-call chain**: `ALWAYS_ALLOW` → lint (`decideLint`) → `decideOutOfStage` → allow/deny. Any
exception inside the plugin **allows** the call.
**Untouched tags are never trimmed** (the safety net for new plugins); `auto` never trims; only an e
xplicit `strict: true` on a stage can override that.
📖 Full runtime logic, data files, defaults and degradation paths: **docs/RUNTIME.md**

ts to

h is exactly

**What it does not do** (read this before installing): it does not shrink the system prompt (that is

A DeepSeek Harness host plugin. No build step, no dependencies.
> `unionEnabled` (multi-domain union) is **@experimental and off by default**; see docs/LIMITS.md.
### How the version requirement is actually evaluated
`package.json` declares `engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.4"`. The real check inside DSH is:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Fact | Meaning |
| It is a **semver range**, not an exact version | Claims that the version must match exactly are wr

ong |
| **`includePrerelease: true`** | Prerelease hosts match too; `-rc.N` needs no special handlin

g |
| **An empty string counts as unmet → install is refused** | Never set `engines.dsh` to `""` |
If it blocks you, DSH reports `incompatible-version` with the unmet packages, and the plugin manager
offers `set_version_exemption` for a specific runtime version (at your own risk).
Runtime data (probe history, your `custom_stages.json`) lives in **`~/.dsh/minimal-router/`**, never

inside
the package — a real dependency install puts the package in a directory that gets replaced o
e package — a real dependency install puts the package in a directory that gets replaced on upgrade.
## Why
DSH sends **every** installed plugin's tool schemas on **every** request. With a few dozen plugins t
hat's 100K+ characters of tool descriptions the model re-reads even when it is just chatting.
This plugin groups tools by name, decides which group the current task needs, and (optionally) **phy
sically removes** the rest from the request — then puts the routing hint on the **tail** of the cont
ext instead of the head, so the prefix stays cacheable.
### "What did it actually do?" — `route_activity`
`route_status` tells you the current state; `route_activity` tells you what happened.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Seven kinds: `switch`, `restrict`, `deny`, `block`, `grant`, `reset`, `degrade`.
Stored in `~/.dsh/m
inimal-router/activity.jsonl`, capped at the last 200 events, so it never grows into another thing t
router/activity.jsonl`, capped at the last 200 events, so it never grows into another thing to read.
### The zero-config path: let the model decide what it needs this turn
**No stage table required.** The built-in `route_use` tool narrows the tool set on demand:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
It keeps the `unity` group plus the base tools, trims everything else, and **restores automatically

after
3 turns** — nothing to remember to undo. `route_use({ "groups": [] })` releases immediately.
Where do group names come from? `route_status` → `tagCounts`. They are derived from tool names, so y

ou never
define a workflow up front.

> **Why not a per-turn judging model?**
> That is one extra request per turn, with the whole context

re-sent at full price. Measured here: 99.9% of
> the tokens this plugin saves are **cache-priced**,

so paying one full-price request to save cheap tokens is
> a net loss. The judgement goes back to t

he model that is already in the context — it knows what it is doing;
> one tool lets it say so, at z

s already in the context — it knows what it is doing;
> one tool lets it say so, at zero extra cost.
### Why not fully automatic?
Because **"never block the wrong tool" outranks "save the most tokens"**.
For any tool group that no stage claims, the only safe default is to **allow it**. Guessing what you
r brand-new tool does would sometimes guess wrong — and a wrong guess blocks you in the middle of a
task, which is far worse than not saving a few thousand tokens.
`route_init` is the compromise: one scan of *your* tools, one template, about a minute of editing, t
hen routing is automatic forever. It lists every unclaimed group with its tool count, so the decisio
n you are confirming is a small, concrete one.
> One line: it is not lazy. Blind guessing is just more expensive than one minute of confirmation.
